strengths: Pixal3D (especially mv_frontback_s7 and sv_gemA_s7) captures micro-silhouettes like the crescent-hook katana guard, distinct corset lacing, and sharp collar flaps much better than TRELLIS.2.
Pixal3D's generated textures provide usable colour separation (red dress, skin, dark hair) that translates cleanly into the 64px sprite pipeline, whereas TRELLIS.2 textures are unusable/black.
mv_frontback_s7 eliminates the hallucinated long ponytails seen in SV runs while preserving the full blade length and thin ribbon structures.
t2cpp_1024_gemA_s7 produces cleaner, smoother clay surfaces on the dress and hair bun with fewer non-manifold artifacts than Pixal3D.
baseline_hunyuan2mini is the only watertight mesh and executes fastest (23s), though its details are too soft for direct detail reference.
weaknesses: Pixal3D SV runs hallucinate long ponytails or thick braids in the back view that ruin rear/side silhouettes in the 64px sprites.
mv_frontback_s7 flattens the sword into the frontal plane and duplicates the hair bun vertically due to 2-view ambiguity.
All Pixal3D meshes are overly dense (~970k tris) with high non-manifold edge counts (3.8k to 26.6k), failing watertightness.
TRELLIS.2 cpp runs suffer from severe texture darkening/blackout (even the 768px fix looks burnt in the sprite sheet) and blunt thin features like the sword blade and collar edges.
sv_iso34_s7 suffers from severe perspective distortion, resulting in squat proportions, a serrated blade, and a melted face.
tuning_suggestions: Run Pixal3D MV with all 4 views (front, back, left, right from chibi_turnaround_v6 with uncapped blade tips) since the weights expect 4 views; this should fix the doubled bun and flat-plane sword in mv_frontback_s7.
Stick to concept-projection colouring for the sprite pipeline rather than baked AI textures, as it yields much cleaner palette snapping across both engines.
For TRELLIS.2 cpp, debug the colour/lighting normalizer on the 1024px pipeline or use vertex-colour transfer from the concept image.
Apply a post-process decimation and manifold-repair pass (e.g., Blender Voxel Remesh or MeshLab) to Pixal3D outputs if boolean/rigging operations are required downstream.
